Goal

Shobu is played on four small boards at once. Every turn you move two of your stones: a quiet move at home, then the same move somewhere else, where it can shove an enemy stone off the edge. Push all four of your opponent's stones off any one board to win.

Rules

The boards

There are four 4×4 boards, given to you as one 8×8 grid of 8 input lines: x is the column (0 to 7, left to right) and y the row (0 to 7, top to bottom). The start position, exactly as your program reads it:

01234567
0wwwwwwwwwhite's home boards
1........
2........
3bbbbbbbb
4wwwwwwwwblack's home boards
5........
6........
7bbbbbbbb
dark boardslight boards
  • The left column of boards (x < 4) is dark, the right column (x ≥ 4) is light.
  • Black's home boards are the two bottom ones (y ≥ 4), white's the two top ones (y < 4).
  • Each player starts with four stones on every board: black on row 3 of each board (y = 3 and 7), white on row 0 (y = 0 and 4).
  • Stones never leave their board, except by being pushed off it.

A turn: two moves

Black moves first. On your turn you make a passive move and then an aggressive move with the same displacement.

  1. Passive move. Pick one of your stones on one of your two home boards and move it 1 or 2 squares in any of the 8 directions (orthogonal or diagonal). Every square it passes over or lands on must be empty: a passive move never touches another stone.
  2. Aggressive move. Then move one of your stones on a board of the other colour (dark ↔ light), on your side or your opponent's, by exactly the same direction and distance. This stone may push:
    • it may push one enemy stone that is in its path or on its landing square;
    • the pushed stone ends up one square past where your stone lands; if that square is off the board, the stone is removed from the game;
    • you may not push your own stone, push two stones, or push a stone onto another stone.

Both moves are made in one turn and given as one output. Only turns whose aggressive move is legal are legal; the list of legal turns is in your input.

End of a round

  • You win the round as soon as one board has no stones of your opponent.
  • A player with no legal turn loses the round.
  • A round that reaches 110 moves (55 each) is a draw.

Pie rule

Moving first can be an advantage, and some first moves are much stronger than others. So in every round, on white's first turn, white may answer SWAP instead of a move: the players exchange colours for the rest of the round.

  • The player who swapped now plays black, with black's first move already on the board.
  • The other player now plays white and moves next.
  • So black's best first move is a balanced one: a first move that is too strong just gets taken by the opponent.

SWAP is offered only on that one turn (it then appears in your list of legal turns); anywhere else it is an invalid action. A swap is not a move: it does not count towards the 110-move limit.

Match

A match is two rounds: you start as black (moving first) in one round and as white in the other, and the pie rule applies in both. A won round is worth 2 points, a draw 1, whichever colour you ended up playing. The player with more points wins the match; equal points are a draw.

Example

  • Opening move. Black plays 3 7 4 3 0 -2. Passive: the stone on (3,7), on black's dark home board, moves two squares up to (3,5) over empty squares. Aggressive: the stone on (4,3), on white's light board (light, so the other colour), moves two squares up to (4,1). Nothing is pushed: white's stone on (4,0) is beyond the landing square.
  • Push off. Later, with that black stone still on (4,1) and the white stone on (4,0), an aggressive move of 0 -1 (one up) lands on (4,0) and pushes the white stone to (4,-1): off the board, so it is removed.
  • Illegal push. A black stone on (4,3) cannot move 0 -1 if white stones stand on both (4,2) and (4,1): that would push two stones in a row.

Game Input

Input for one game turn

Line 1: round (0 or 1) and myColor, the colour you play this turn (0 black: home boards at the bottom; 1 white). It can change during a round, after a swap.
Next 8 lines: the rows of the grid, top to bottom, 8 characters each: . empty, b black stone, w white stone.
Next line: your opponent's last turn as px py ax ay dx dy, SWAP if your opponent just swapped, or - at the start of a round.
Next line: moveCount, the number of legal turns.
Next moveCount lines: a legal turn px py ax ay dx dy. On white's first turn of a round the last of these lines is SWAP.

Output

One line: px py ax ay dx dy — move your stone at (px,py) by (dx,dy) as the passive move, then your stone at (ax,ay) by the same (dx,dy) as the aggressive move. (dx,dy) is one or two steps in one of 8 directions, for example 0 -2 (two up) or -1 1 (one diagonally down-left). Anything after the six numbers is shown as a message.
Or, on white's first turn of a round only: SWAP (optionally followed by a message).

Constraints

Response time for the first turn ≤ 1000 ms
Response time for one turn ≤ 100 ms
moveCount ≤ 1025

Leagues

Each league has a boss to beat:

  • Wood 4: a greedy bot. It takes a winning move if it sees one, otherwise the move that removes the most material, and never looks at your reply.
  • Wood 3: Monte Carlo tree search with short random playouts. It also recognises positions it has fully solved.
  • Wood 2: a plain three-move-deep minimax with alpha-beta pruning, counting stones.

The bosses never swap. Wood 1 is the top league.

Shobu is played on four small boards at once. Every turn you move two of your stones: a quiet move at home, then the same move somewhere else, where it can shove an enemy stone off the edge. Push all four of your opponent's stones off any one board to win.

Rules

The boards

There are four 4×4 boards, given to you as one 8×8 grid of 8 input lines: x is the column (0 to 7, left to right) and y the row (0 to 7, top to bottom). The start position, exactly as your program reads it:

01234567
0wwwwwwwwwhite's home boards
1........
2........
3bbbbbbbb
4wwwwwwwwblack's home boards
5........
6........
7bbbbbbbb
dark boardslight boards
  • The left column of boards (x < 4) is dark, the right column (x ≥ 4) is light.
  • Black's home boards are the two bottom ones (y ≥ 4), white's the two top ones (y < 4).
  • Each player starts with four stones on every board: black on row 3 of each board (y = 3 and 7), white on row 0 (y = 0 and 4).
  • Stones never leave their board, except by being pushed off it.

A turn: two moves

Black moves first. On your turn you make a passive move and then an aggressive move with the same displacement.

  1. Passive move. Pick one of your stones on one of your two home boards and move it 1 or 2 squares in any of the 8 directions (orthogonal or diagonal). Every square it passes over or lands on must be empty: a passive move never touches another stone.
  2. Aggressive move. Then move one of your stones on a board of the other colour (dark ↔ light), on your side or your opponent's, by exactly the same direction and distance. This stone may push:
    • it may push one enemy stone that is in its path or on its landing square;
    • the pushed stone ends up one square past where your stone lands; if that square is off the board, the stone is removed from the game;
    • you may not push your own stone, push two stones, or push a stone onto another stone.

Both moves are made in one turn and given as one output. Only turns whose aggressive move is legal are legal; the list of legal turns is in your input.

End of a round

  • You win the round as soon as one board has no stones of your opponent.
  • A player with no legal turn loses the round.
  • A round that reaches 110 moves (55 each) is a draw.

Pie rule

Moving first can be an advantage, and some first moves are much stronger than others. So in every round, on white's first turn, white may answer SWAP instead of a move: the players exchange colours for the rest of the round.

  • The player who swapped now plays black, with black's first move already on the board.
  • The other player now plays white and moves next.
  • So black's best first move is a balanced one: a first move that is too strong just gets taken by the opponent.

SWAP is offered only on that one turn (it then appears in your list of legal turns); anywhere else it is an invalid action. A swap is not a move: it does not count towards the 110-move limit.

Match

A match is two rounds: you start as black (moving first) in one round and as white in the other, and the pie rule applies in both. A won round is worth 2 points, a draw 1, whichever colour you ended up playing. The player with more points wins the match; equal points are a draw.

Example

  • Opening move. Black plays 3 7 4 3 0 -2. Passive: the stone on (3,7), on black's dark home board, moves two squares up to (3,5) over empty squares. Aggressive: the stone on (4,3), on white's light board (light, so the other colour), moves two squares up to (4,1). Nothing is pushed: white's stone on (4,0) is beyond the landing square.
  • Push off. Later, with that black stone still on (4,1) and the white stone on (4,0), an aggressive move of 0 -1 (one up) lands on (4,0) and pushes the white stone to (4,-1): off the board, so it is removed.
  • Illegal push. A black stone on (4,3) cannot move 0 -1 if white stones stand on both (4,2) and (4,1): that would push two stones in a row.

Game Input

Input for one game turn

Line 1: round (0 or 1) and myColor, the colour you play this turn (0 black: home boards at the bottom; 1 white). It can change during a round, after a swap.
Next 8 lines: the rows of the grid, top to bottom, 8 characters each: . empty, b black stone, w white stone.
Next line: your opponent's last turn as px py ax ay dx dy, SWAP if your opponent just swapped, or - at the start of a round.
Next line: moveCount, the number of legal turns.
Next moveCount lines: a legal turn px py ax ay dx dy. On white's first turn of a round the last of these lines is SWAP.

Output

One line: px py ax ay dx dy — move your stone at (px,py) by (dx,dy) as the passive move, then your stone at (ax,ay) by the same (dx,dy) as the aggressive move. (dx,dy) is one or two steps in one of 8 directions, for example 0 -2 (two up) or -1 1 (one diagonally down-left). Anything after the six numbers is shown as a message.
Or, on white's first turn of a round only: SWAP (optionally followed by a message).

Constraints

Response time for the first turn ≤ 1000 ms
Response time for one turn ≤ 100 ms
moveCount ≤ 1025

Leagues

Each league has a boss to beat:

  • Wood 4: a greedy bot. It takes a winning move if it sees one, otherwise the move that removes the most material, and never looks at your reply.
  • Wood 3: Monte Carlo tree search with short random playouts. It also recognises positions it has fully solved.
  • Wood 2: a plain three-move-deep minimax with alpha-beta pruning, counting stones.

The bosses never swap. Wood 1 is the top league.

lastMove: your opponent's last move as "px py ax ay dx dy", SWAP if your opponent just swapped, or - at the start of a round
moveCount: number of legal moves
move: a legal move "px py ax ay dx dy"; on white's first turn of a round the last one is SWAP (pie rule)

OUTPUT
px py ax ay dx dy: move your stone at (px,py) on one of your home boards by (dx,dy), then your stone at (ax,ay) on a board of the other colour by the same (dx,dy); or SWAP on white's first turn of a round; optionally followed by a message
